parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit fails: the two files don't follow one consistent abstraction or boundary. BoxOffice.ts works through narrow store abstractions (EventStore, TicketStore). It rebuilds domain entities (Event, Ticket) and leaves the invariants to them: Event.sell enforces capacity and Ticket.admit enforces single admission. GateLog.ts skips that pattern. It takes PrismaService, the raw client, and calls prisma.scan.create / prisma.scan.findMany directly, with no store and no domain entity. Scanning is also split across both files. BoxOffice.admit calls ticket.admit(...) and tickets.markScanned(...). GateLog.scanned writes its own separate scan record, keyed `${gate}:${code}`, without checking that the ticket exists or obeying Ticket.admit's rules. So the "a ticket is scanned" fact is recorded in two places that can disagree. There is also a smaller duplication inside BoxOffice.ts: the EventStore row-to-Event mapping (new Event(d.id, d.title, d.venueCapacity, d.seatsSold, d.startsAt, d.priceCents)) is repeated in purchase() and listing() instead of living in one place. This judgment is about consistent abstraction, not import direction, which is out of scope.

violations.message: Skips the module's store and domain-entity abstraction by using PrismaService (prisma.scan.create/findMany) directly, while BoxOffice uses EventStore/TicketStore with Event/Ticket entities.

GateLog.scanned records ticket scans separately from BoxOffice.admit (Ticket.admit + TicketStore.markScanned), so scan/admission state is split across two places and the single-admission rule is not applied.
The row-to-Event mapping (new Event(d.id, d.title, d.venueCapacity, d.seatsSold, d.startsAt, d.priceCents)) is repeated in purchase() and listing() instead of being in one place.
